A B S T R A C T
Cobalt electrodeposition is the core technology in chip manufacturing. Butynediol (BD) is the key component in
cobalt electrodeposition. In this work, the molecule structure and adsorption ability of BD are successfully
revealed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The number of transferred electrons (ΔN) value near 0,
and the interaction between oxygen atom not alkynyl group in BD and cobalt, demonstrating that BD is phys-
ically adsorbed on the cobalt surface. The adsorption energy of BD on hexagonal closepacked (hcp)(101) is
−0.67 eV, which is the highest adsorption energy among crystal faces, manifesting that (101) may be a potential
preferred orientation. Then the effects of BD on the electroreduction behavior of cobalt is revealed by electro
chemical experimental techniques. BD can inhibit the electroreduction of cobalt ions based on kinetics and
decreases the diffusion coefficient from 3.43 × 10<sup>−</sup> <sup>6</sup> to 1.33 × 10<sup>−</sup> <sup>6</sup> cm<sup>2</sup>/s, but the reaction is irreversible with
diffusion control whether it contains BD or not. BD can make the charge transfer resistance increase from 241
Ω/cm<sup>2</sup> to 496 Ω/cm<sup>2</sup>. BD has some effects on the cobalt electroreduction kinetics, it does not change the
instantaneous nucleation mechanism. Finally, the morphology, composition and structure of the cobalt coating
are characterized by scanning electron microscope (SEM) with energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray
diffraction (XRD). BD can refine the grains and improving the uniformity of the cobalt coating. Although the
properties of the mixed crystals have not changed, the preferred orientation has changed due to the addition of
BD. A new peak of hcp(101) arises resulted from the adsorption of BD to form a retained surface, which are
consistent with the calculation results. And the relatively positive values of stress change indicates that BD causes
the internal stress of cobalt coating to be tensile stress.

Metal cobalt interconnect layer is mainly prepared by electrodepo-

suppression effect and made cobalt a three-dimensional nucleation. Wu

inhibitor to achieve nanometer scale superfilling of cobalt electrode
position. Kiruba et al. [14] presented that butynediol (BD) would change
the interfacial pH to regulate and control the formation of cobalt. It is
worth noting that BD as a typical type-II brightener has attracted much
attention among the many cobalt additives. Jeyabharathi et al. [15]
deemed that BD would cause electrochemical oscillation due to the
hydrogenation of BD during cobalt electrodeposition. Pan et al. [16]
showed that BD and saccharin together could decrease the microhard
ness of cobalt deposits as a result of increased grain size. Although it is
well known that BD can be used as an additive, the effect of its molecular
structure on the interface of cobalt electrodeposition has not been
elucidated at a molecular level. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out
relevant research. This study demonstrates the adsorption state of BD on
cobalt surface and the effects of adsorption on crystal growth and
orientation. This enriches the understanding of the role of additives in
the cobalt electrodeposition process, revealing that BD achieves uni-
formity and compact film morphology through interactions with the
cobalt surface, which is conducive to promote the development of
high-performance chip interconnection technology.

3.2. Electrostatic potential and average local ionisation energy
Adsorption can be divided into physical adsorption and chemical
adsorption, which are related to the electrostatic effects and the reac-
tivity of molecule, respectively. To expound the electrostatic effects of
BD, the colored isopleth maps of the ESP and the area distribution of ESP
spacings on the equivalent surface for BD are displayed in Fig. 2. The red
region and blue region represent the higher and lower ESP, respectively.
The maximum and minimum values of ESP are expressed by orange and
cyan spheres, respectively. As shown in Fig. 2a, it can be seen that the
lower ESP is mainly distributed on the oxygen atoms on both sides, and
the higher ESP is mainly located in the hydrogen atoms on both sides,
indicating that the electrons are mainly concentrated on the oxygen
atoms on both sides, and the holes are primarily distributed in the
hydrogen atoms on both sides. The highest and lowest ESP values are
52.67 and −43.90 kcal/mol. This uneven distribution of ESP can easily
lead to a strong electrostatic effect [33]. Fig. 2b presents the histogram
of the area distribution at different ESP intervals for BD. Obviously, BD
has a relatively high percentage of area in the low (< −30) and high
(>10) regions of ESP. The results again manifest that BD can be adsor-
bed on metal substances in a strong electrostatic interaction [33], and is
mainly physically adsorbed by oxygen atoms.
To clarify the reactivity of BD, the ALIE is completed and the results
are presented in Fig. 3. The lower the value of ALIE is, the stronger the
reactivity is. The cyan spheres represent the lower points of ALIE, which
means that these points are easy to attack by electrophilic reaction [33].
The highest and lowest ALIE values are 268.89 and 203.39 kcal/mol.
Obviously, the reactive sites are mainly located in the alkynyl group,

3.3. Adsorption on cobalt surface
Based on the ESP and ALIE results, it can be found that BD may be
chemical and physical adsorption, and the adsorption regions are
concentrated at the alkynyl group and the oxygen atoms on both sides,
respectively. To further understand the adsorption type of BD, the
adsorption structure of BD and its adsorption energy on different crystal
faces are completed. Cobalt possesses face centered cubic (fcc) and
hexagonal closepacked (hcp) structures. Fig. 4 presents the adsorption
behavior of BD on different fcc and hcp crystal faces. Table 1 and Table 2
show the energy values of the different structures and the corresponding
adsorptions, respectively. As shown in Fig. 4, regardless of crystal faces,
BD is adsorbed exothermically. At the co-adsorbed structure, there are
